title: EEMS Platform — Architecture & Trust
seo_title: EEMS Platform — Architecture & Trust | Achala IT Solutions
meta_description: Architecture, security posture and compliance evidence for EEMS Platform — Decision Intelligence Hub from Achala IT Solutions.

blocks.x: EEMS Platform — Architecture & Trust in production terms — the runtime that holds it, the policies that bound it, the dashboards that prove it, and the quarterly delta your finance team can bank.

The platform separates three planes. The data plane carries workload (one governed entry point with SLA guarantees, versioned decision policies with effective-dating and simulation, shadow scoring and incremental traffic shifting); the control plane carries policy and orchestration (full input/model/policy snapshots per decision, online feature store with point-in-time correctness); the evidence plane carries audit, replay and conformity documentation — the plane most vendors skip and every regulator asks about.

blocks.title: EEMS Platform — deployment topology and flow
blocks.note: What runs at the edge is chosen by physics, not fashion: latency, bandwidth and autonomy constraints decide placement — and the fleet is managed as one estate.

blocks.x: Nexus runs inside your security perimeter with customer-managed keys, full audit export and evidence packs mapped to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and model-risk expectations. Decision policies, model versions and feature states are immutable artifacts — the replay trail is cryptographic, not testimonial.

items: The control estate mapped to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 criteria, evidence produced continuously.
Sector rules translated into controls per jurisdiction — the mapping is data, reviewed when the regime moves.
AI-specific obligations mapped to controls — model risk, transparency and human oversight, owned by name.

blocks.x: The envelope is explicit: per-tenant quotas, latency budgets on the decision path, and throughput targets reviewed at every load test — sizing is a contract, not a hope.
Telemetry your control owner sees weekly — the same numbers at every gate:

items: Query latency measured at p95 from real workloads — the number users feel is the number reported.
Batch windows measured against the plan every run — the number reported is the observed one.
Up 97–98.6% of tables inside their declared window per workflow, reported weekly against the signed baseline
Deployed inside your tenancy, your keys, your logs — the default for regulated estates.
Operated by us under contract — SLOs published, changes gated, your auditors given a walkthrough path.
Split by design: what must stay local stays local, what benefits from scale scales.
